title: Evolution proposal
description: One candidate edit to one skill, with the evidence that motivated it. Written by scripts/propose.py, checked by scripts/validate.py, and the only artifact a model is allowed to produce. A proposal that does not satisfy this schema is refused rather than repaired.

id.description: Cycle id plus the candidate's index within that cycle, for example 2026-10-3.

cycle.description: The cycle this proposal belongs to, by year and month.

skill.description: The skill being changed, as the directory name under skills/.

class.description: What kind of change this is. The class decides which paths are in scope; validate.py refuses a class whose changed files do not match it.

evidence.description: Why this change is proposed. At least one citation, and every citation must resolve at the pinned commit or the proposal is refused with exit 2.

kind.description: What sort of evidence this is. signal cites a signals/ observation, ledger a prior cycle's record, receipt a gate receipt, git a commit or a diff window.

path.description: Repository-relative path the citation resolves against. Required for signal and git citations.

line.description: Line number within path, for a signal or git citation that names one.

id.description: The ledger row id or receipt id, for those kinds.

observed.description: The measurement itself, in one sentence, as the loop read it. This is what a reviewer checks by hand.

files.description: Every repository-relative path the patch touches. validate.py refuses any path outside the skill's own directory, and refuses a persona, command, count or workflow file outright.

diff_sha256.description: Hash of the patch, which is how a rejected diff is recognised and not proposed again inside the two cycle window.

rationale.description: Plain prose, for the human who has to decide. Not a restatement of the diff.

cost.description: What this candidate cost, recorded by lane.py at the moment of the call rather than reconstructed afterwards.

validation.description: Written by validate.py, never by the proposer. Absent until the proposal has been checked.

reason.description: Why, in the guard's own words. For a refusal this is the text a human reads, so it names the rule and the offending path or citation.
